channel.title: The Minnesota Star Tribune - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Minnesota Star Tribune (startribune.com)

item.title: As J.J. McCarthy nears return, Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell takes himself to task for offense’s woes
item.description: O’Connell said McCarthy is “symptom free” from a Nov. 23 concussion and expected to start Sunday vs. Washington.

item.title: Large mobile home park on edge of Twin Cities at center of affordability dispute
item.description: A legal dispute raises allegations of a misinformation campaign and a conflict over the majority of the affordable housing in Corcoran.

item.title: Two DJs stalked by the same listener. Is a life of terror the price of being in the public eye?
item.description: What made Mary Lucia and Jade Tittle so good at their jobs also brought a decade of abuse. Our desire to “know” on-air personalities puts women, especially, at risk.

item.title: With federal oversight waning, Minnesota AG scrutinizes buy-now-pay-later loan firms
item.description: Minnesota and six other states are asking the companies for information on billing, credit reporting and late fee collection.

item.title: Shooting in St. Paul’s East Side injures four people
item.description: None of the victims’ injuries were life-threatening.

item.title: Neal: Justin Jefferson has every right to be frustrated, but he shouldn’t stay silent
item.description: The face of the Vikings franchise, declined to speak to reporters after Sunday’s shutout loss to the Seahawks.

item.title: Two more craft breweries to close in Twin Cities suburbs
item.description: Invictus in Blaine and Schram Haus in Chaska succumbed to industrywide challenges, but the latter’s beer will live on at its sister winery.

item.title: Gophers women’s basketball dominates at home against Samford
item.description: The Gophers led 35-9 at halftime to improve to 5-0 at Williams Arena on the season.

item.title: Former Minneapolis Chamber CEO pleads guilty to mail fraud in embezzlement case
item.description: Jonathan Weinhagen admitted to taking more than $200,000 from the chamber. He could serve between 27 and 33 months in prison.

item.title: Trump administration to investigate Minnesota over claims of fraud pipeline to terrorists
item.description: DFL Gov. Tim Walz has said he welcomes a federal investigation.
